_neon_ask_note: The Neon MCP server ignores the client's ?readonly=true URL param when the OAuth grant made at session start is full-scope: verified live 2026-08-24, a freshly-authed session reported 'Write mode active. Destructive tools are exposed.' and exposed delete_branch/delete_project/run_sql/reset_from_parent with full schemas even though ~/.claude.json wires ?readonly=true and 50-mcp.json's deniedMcpServers blocks the full-access URL (see that file's _neon_note) -- the OAuth SCOPE beat the URL parameter. Owner decision: keep the write tools usable rather than deny them or attempt to re-scope OAuth -- this permissions.ask rule is the real gate, pausing every matching call for an explicit yes/no instead of letting it land silently. Verb globs (delete*/create*/run_sql*/reset*/prepare*/complete*/provision*/configure*/update*/grant*/revoke*/set_*/add_*/remove_*/rename*/transfer*) catch tools Neon adds later by pattern rather than requiring an enumeration update; the explicit tool names are listed too as belt-and-braces in case a future tool's verb doesn't fit one of the globs. Read tools (list_*, describe_*, get_*, explain_*, query_logs, search, fetch) are deliberately NOT listed here, EXCEPT credential-returning tools, which are ask-gated even though they share the get_* shape -- see the CRITICAL note below. CAST v10 sec1 hardening (2026-08-24), two gaps closed after security reproduced both live against this file: CRITICAL -- mcp__neon__get_connection_string returns a LIVE Postgres connection string with an embedded password; it starts with 'get_' so it was previously excluded here as a read tool and produced zero signal, identical to list_projects. 'Returns a secret' is not 'mutates data', so it is ask-gated via the explicit get_connection_string literal entry (belt-and-braces), kept separate from the verb-glob list above so the two risk classes stay legible both here and in cast-pretool-dispatch.py's _classify_neon_risk. STRUCTURAL correction (2026-08-24, 3rd pass, after security BLOCKED this guard twice): the *credential*/*password*/*connection* MID-STRING globs originally added alongside that entry have been REMOVED -- they are almost certainly INERT, since docs/architecture/enforcement-awareness-split.md characterises this engine's native permission matching as 'Prefix-glob matching' and grepping managed-settings.d/*.json finds zero other precedent for a mid-string wildcard, only prefix/trailing forms (update*, grant*, delete*, etc). Keeping them would have been false reassurance. This file therefore does NOT claim coverage of 'any plausible credential/password/connection-shaped tool name' -- it covers only the literal names enumerated below (get_connection_string today). The actual fail-closed guarantee for an unenumerated future credential-shaped tool now lives entirely in cast-pretool-dispatch.py's _classify_neon_risk, hardened in the same pass to an EXACT enumeration of known-safe reads (its list_.*/describe_.*/explain_.*/get_.* wildcards removed) with default-unsafe for everything else, plus get_neon_auth_config dropped from that safe list (unverified response shape, security MEDIUM). See tests/cast-neon-notify-guard.bats's drift tests for the cross-check that keeps this file and that classifier from silently diverging. DISCLOSURE (2026-08-24, security pass closing a gap in this note itself -- the pass otherwise cleared with 0 Critical/0 High): this ask list does NOT prompt for the credential-shaped get_*/describe_*/list_*/explain_* risk class beyond the single literal get_connection_string entry above -- none of the ten previously-reproduced bypass names (get_client_secret, get_database_uri, get_api_key, get_bearer_token, get_jwt, get_oauth_token, describe_api_token, describe_secret_key, list_role_secrets, explain_token_scope) matches any entry or glob here, so a call using one of those names, or any future name in that shape, executes with NO interactive confirmation from this file -- the human is never asked to confirm before it runs. Those names ARE still classified non-safe and notified+recorded by cast-pretool-dispatch.py's _classify_neon_risk (the fail-closed exact enumeration described above), so the guarantee for this risk class is 'recorded, not interrupted': the human learns from a post-hoc desktop notification and the egress ledger, after the call has already executed, not from a prompt before it runs. This is a stated, accepted trade, not a claim of parity with the ask-gated verbs above -- it avoids bloating this list with an unbounded set of unconfirmed credential-shaped tool names, and a general fix is hard for two structural reasons already covered in this note: the native permission engine's matching is prefix-glob only (no content/mid-string wildcard, per the STRUCTURAL correction above), and ask is checked before allow (see the precedence paragraph below), so a broad ask-everything mcp__neon__* rule would also catch every safe read with no way to carve an exception back out. Do not read this file as prompting for every non-safe Neon call -- it prompts only for the verb globs and literal names enumerated in permissions.ask above. HIGH -- the verb-glob set above was missing update*/grant*/revoke*/set_*/add_*/remove_*/rename*/transfer*; security reproduced mcp__neon__grant_access and mcp__neon__update_project producing zero signal, and both are now covered (globs plus explicit belt-and-braces entries). Companion notify+record guard (fires even for a dispatched subagent, which never sees this prompt): scripts/cast-pretool-dispatch.py's _notify_neon_risk / _classify_neon_risk -- that side is now FAIL-CLOSED (flags anything NOT in its known-safe-read allowlist) rather than enumerating dangerous verbs, so a tool Neon adds tomorrow gets signal by default even before this JSON fragment is updated; this file stays allowlist-shaped because permissions.ask/allow are globs with no negation operator, so a pure denylist can't be expressed here. Investigated switching to 'ask on mcp__neon__* plus allow the known-safe reads' instead (would need no enumeration here at all): rejected because docs/architecture/enforcement-awareness-split.md:55 records the native precedence as deny -> ask -> allow -> prompt, i.e. ask is checked BEFORE allow, so a broad ask-everything rule would catch every read before a narrower allow exception ever got a chance to match -- the same 'a broad rule from a higher-precedence category cannot carry a narrower exception from a lower one' shape already documented there for deny/allow. Widening the existing allowlist (this file) was the only option left. cast-merge-settings.sh deep-merges the permissions dict per-key, so this file must define ONLY 'ask' -- it must never also define 'allow' or 'deny', which live solely in 10-permissions.json / 11-deny.json respectively (a second fragment defining the same array key silently clobbers the first, per that script's merge() docstring).

_neon_note: mcpServers here is INERT: Claude Code reads MCP servers only from ~/.claude.json, .mcp.json, or /Library/Application Support/ClaudeCode/managed-mcp.json — never from settings.json. This file's mcpServers key is retained solely to propagate removals. The read-only Neon server (https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp?readonly=true) is wired at user scope in ~/.claude.json. The deniedMcpServers entries above block the full read-write Neon endpoint: the serverUrl entry is the real enforcement and was verified by live probe on 2026-08-24 to block https://mcp.neon.tech/mcp while sparing the ?readonly=true URL, so it survives a connector rename and also catches a second server aimed at the same endpoint; the serverName entry is a secondary catch. RESIDUAL, stated plainly: a full-access Neon URL carrying some OTHER query string (e.g. ?projectId=x) would not match the serverUrl entry, and a denied server disappears from `claude mcp list` with no warning, so a deny that stops matching is silent in both directions. Verified against code.claude.com/docs/en/mcp and /managed-mcp.

_sandbox_note: PARTIALLY LIVE (updated 2026-07-02, CC 2.1.195): filesystem denyRead DOES enforce in sessions where CC engages the Seatbelt sandbox — proven by EPERM on cast.db reads in a live interactive session (2026-07-02 doctor probe). Enforcement is session/permission-mode-dependent: explicitly-allowed and bypass-permissions commands run unsandboxed, so probes from autonomous sessions may observe no denial — verify from an interactive default-mode session. excludedCommands does NOT bypass filesystem.denyRead. filesystem.allowRead wins over denyRead: cast.db is allowlisted (Ed decision 2026-07-02) so cast status and /doctor read real data; history.jsonl, logs/**, and routing-log.jsonl stay denied. The egress PreToolUse hook (logs/egress.jsonl) remains the only live egress enforcement. Note: CC does not natively read managed-settings.d/; cast-merge-settings.sh merges this into ~/.claude/settings.json (user layer, not tamper-proof MDM). Verify ENFORCEMENT, not key-presence.
